title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a typescript copy of what appears to be Deligne's 'Courbes elliptiques : formulaire (d'après J. Tate)', published in Modular Functions of One Variable IV (LNM 476, 1975). The section numbering and formulas match that text. The page contains no original Grothendieck mathematics beyond possible marginal annotations.

End of Section 2 (2 and 3 invertible).
- Every genus-1 curve with a section and an invertible invariant differential π can be put uniquely in the form Y² = 4X³ − g₂X − g₃ with π = dX/Y.
- So Spec Z[1/6][g₂,g₃] is a fine moduli scheme for pairs (E,π). Fineness follows from the rigidification remark: an automorphism preserving π has u = 1, and the normalization a₁ = a₂ = a₃ = 0 then forces r = s = t = 0.
- From c₄ = 12g₂, c₆ = 216g₃ and Δ = g₂³ − 27g₃² one gets c₄³ − c₆² = 1728Δ. This is a polynomial identity in the aᵢ, so it holds over Z and hence in every characteristic.

Section 3 (2 and c₄ invertible).
- With 2 invertible one can complete the square, so a₁ = a₃ = 0. This gives y² = x³ + a₂x² + a₄x + a₆.
- The remaining coordinate changes are the translations x ↦ x + r, i.e. u = 1, s = t = 0.
- One has b₂ = 4a₂, b₄ = 2a₄, b₆ = 4a₆ and d₆ = 8(a₂a₄ − 9a₆).
- c₄ = 2⁴(a₂² − 3a₄).
- −c₆ = 2⁶a₂³ − 2⁵3²a₂a₄ + 2⁵3³a₆.
- Δ = 2⁴δ, where δ is the discriminant of the cubic.

The next page shows that d₆ transforms affinely in r with linear coefficient c₄. Check: a₂'a₄' − 9a₆' = a₂a₄ − 9a₆ + 2(a₂² − 3a₄)r. So when c₄ is invertible there is a unique normalization d₆ = 0. This yields the fine moduli scheme over Z[1/2] in Proposition 3.5 on the next page, serving the same purpose: explicit moduli of elliptic curves with a trivialized ω away from small primes.
errors: No mathematical errors found. All formulas were checked: c₄, c₆, d₆ (as b₂b₄ − 18b₆), Δ = 16·disc, and 1728Δ = c₄³ − c₆² via g₂ = c₄/12, g₃ = c₆/216.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a copy of the Deligne/Tate 'Formulaire' (published 1975), apparently filed among Grothendieck's papers. It is standard and fully published. The only unpublished trace is the brief marginal note ('9', 'section e'), whose author is uncertain; 'section e' presumably refers to the identity section.
transcription_corrections: 'homogōnes' in the typescript should read 'homogènes' (a typing slip; the machine transcription itself is fine).

Handwritten '9' near the title and at the bottom-left is archival page numbering. The handwritten marginal note reads 'section e', which plausibly refers to the identity section of the universal curve.
The formula (2.6) line in the image reads 'c₄³ − c₆² = 1728 Δ'; the transcription is correct.
